summary:
With many range-sum questions on the same data, precompute prefix sums once: `prefix[k]` = total of the
first k days. Then the total from day l to day r is `prefix[r + 1] − prefix[l]`, one subtraction per query.
O(n + q) instead of O(n · q).

question.md:
For each query `[l, r]`, return `sales[l] + … + sales[r]` (both ends included), in query order.

- **Many queries on unchanged data:** up to 10⁵ queries over up to 10⁵ days. Summing each range directly
  could take 10¹⁰ steps.
- **Big numbers:** values reach ±10⁹ and a range can contain 10⁵ of them, so totals reach ±10¹⁴. Use
  64-bit integers for the prefix sums (`[10⁹, 10⁹]` already sums past the 32-bit limit).
- **Single-day queries** like `[3, 3]` are allowed.

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- A query with `l = r` is a single day.
- Totals can reach `10⁵ × 10⁹ = 10¹⁴` in size: use 64-bit sums.
- Up to 10⁵ queries, so each must be answered quickly.

think.md:
**Prefix sums.** Let `P[k]` be the sum of the first `k` elements (`P[0] = 0`). Then the sum of any stretch
`a[i .. j−1]` is `P[j] − P[i]`: everything up to `j`, minus everything before `i`. One O(n) pass builds `P`; after
that, every range sum costs O(1). Many "subarray sum" questions become questions about **pairs of prefix sums**.

lines.text: Each query walks its whole range, adding in 64 bits.

complexity.md: **Time O(n · q)** in the worst case: 10¹⁰ additions for 10⁵ long queries. **Space O(q)** for the answers.

limits.md: Overlapping queries re-add the same days. Precomputing prefix sums once answers every query in O(1).

idea.md:
Build `P` once. Answer each query `[l, r]` with `P[r + 1] − P[l]`.

**Why it's right.** `P[r + 1]` covers days `0 … r`; subtracting `P[l]` removes days `0 … l − 1`, leaving
exactly `l … r`.

lines.text: Running totals, one longer than the input so `prefix[0]` is the empty sum. 64-bit, because totals reach 10¹⁴.
Days l … r = (first r + 1 days) − (first l days).

notes.c: Free the prefix array; the caller frees `out`.

complexity.md: **Time O(n + q).** **Space O(n)** for the prefix sums.

steps.text: prefix[k] = total of the first k days; prefix[0] = 0.

walk.title: Build prefix sums once; each query is then one subtraction.

takeaways.md:
- **Many range-sum queries on a fixed array:** prefix sums, O(1) per query.
- The leading `P[0] = 0` removes the special case for `l = 0`.
- **Pitfall:** off-by-one (`P[r] − P[l]` misses day `r`); 32-bit overflow.
